📅 3 August 2026 | 🗳️ Motion to proceed filed

Summary: The bill would extend through the end of 2028 duty-free trade benefits that allow most exports from eligible sub-Saharan African countries to enter the U.S. market without tariffs, while also extending customs user fees through the end of 2031. It would also allow for refunds of duties paid on African imports that entered the country after September 30, 2025.

S. 494 | National Plan for Epilepsy Act | Sen. Eric Schmitt (R-MO) | Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions Committee

📅 4 August 2026 | ✅🏛️ Passed Senate with amendment (unanimous consent)
What's next: To the House (if and when it takes it up)

Summary: The bill would require the federal government to develop a comprehensive national plan to prevent, diagnose, treat, and cure epilepsy, coordinating research and services across all federal agencies. It would also establish an advisory council to evaluate federally funded epilepsy efforts and report to Congress every two years, with the entire initiative set to expire at the end of 2035.

S. 4472 | Accelerating Access to Critical Therapies for ALS Reauthorization Act of 2026 | Sen. Lisa Murkowski (R-AK) | Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions Committee

📅 4 August 2026 | ✅🏛️ Passed Senate with amendment (voice vote)
What's next: To the House (if and when it takes it up)

Summary: The bill would extend funding through fiscal year 2031 for federal research and development programs aimed at finding treatments for ALS and other neurodegenerative diseases, including grants from the National Institutes of Health and Food and Drug Administration as well as a public-private partnership supporting drug development. It would also add new requirements for tracking the safety and effectiveness of investigational drugs, ensure timely reporting of clinical trial safety data, require the FDA to publish five-year development plans for neurodegenerative disease treatments every five years, and mandate reports on the program's impact.
